title: Robust Strange Metallicity across Attractive and Repulsive Hubbard Models
authors: Xiaoyue Ma, Emily Z. Zhang, Thomas P. Devereaux
abstract: Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we compare charge transport in the two-dimensional attractive and repulsive Hubbard models at strong coupling, $|U|/t=6$. Although the interaction with opposite signs generates qualitatively different low-energy spin, charge, and pairing correlations, both exhibit approximately linear-in-temperature resistivity over a broad intermediate- and high-temperature regime. At asymptotically high temperature this common behavior follows from the moment expansion of the conductivity, whose leading contribution is even in $U$. More strikingly, the similarity persists to temperatures well below $|U|$, where strong interaction-dependent correlations have already developed, and also irrespective of whether resistivity crosses the MIR limit. Using the Nernst--Einstein relation, we find that the common linear-in-temperature resistivity is primarily associated with an approximately Curie-like charge compressibility and weakly temperature-dependent diffusivity. The two models separate only at lower temperatures, where the attractive model develops a pronounced feature in the charge diffusivity correlated with signatures of pair formation. These results show that linear-in-temperature incoherent transport in the Hubbard model can be remarkably insensitive to the microscopic nature of the low-energy correlations. Our results suggest that transport in the incoherent regime appears insensitive to what the system will ultimately become at low temperature; the distinction between competing low-energy states becomes visible only when their characteristic correlations acquire sufficiently long spatial or temporal coherence.
summary: This work uses DQMC simulations to compare charge transport in attractive and repulsive Hubbard models at strong coupling. The authors find that both models exhibit strange-metal behavior ($ho \propto T$) over a wide temperature range, suggesting this linear resistivity is a generic feature of incoherent transport rather than being dictated by the system's ultimate low-temperature state. The distinction between the two models only becomes apparent at much lower temperatures.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of 'strange metallicity,' characterized by linear-in-temperature resistivity, in strongly correlated electron systems.
main_result: The linear-in-temperature resistivity observed in both attractive and repulsive Hubbard models is robust and appears insensitive to the microscopic nature of the low-energy correlations.
method: The research employs Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations combined with the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) method for analytic continuation of current-current correlators.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional Hubbard model, analyzed in both attractive ($U<0$) and repulsive ($U>0$) regimes at strong coupling ($|U|/t=6$).
key_observables: DC longitudinal resistivity ($ho_{xx}$), charge compressibility ($\chi_c$), and charge diffusivity ($D$).
important_parameters: Strong coupling regime ($|U|/t=6$), temperature dependence across intermediate and high-temperature regimes, and comparison between $U<0$ and $U>0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Nernst–Einstein relation connecting resistivity to compressibility and diffusivity, and the high-temperature behavior is analyzed via moment expansion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of resistivity ($ho_{xx}$) for both interaction signs, showing the common linear-T behavior, and also plot the temperature dependence of $\chi^{-1}$ and $D^{-1}$ separately.
paper_structure: The paper compares transport properties in the attractive and repulsive Hubbard models across various temperatures, establishing the common linear-T resistivity in the incoherent regime, and then analyzing the low-temperature deviations where the models separate.
why_interesting: The finding that transport linearity is robust across different low-energy correlation types suggests a universal transport constraint in the incoherent regime, which is a general concept applicable to many-body dynamics.
